prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a top-down garage workspace where no other people are present, showing the camera wearer looking down at their own chest, arms, and vehicle wheel hub components positioned between 0.1 and 0.6 metres away above a floor roughly 1.2 to 1.5 metres below. Across frames 1 to 4, an overhead dark bar with 'bluelON' text cuts diagonally across the upper foreground at roughly 0.15 to 0.25 metres from the lens, partially occluding the suspension strut and brake backing plate about 0.3 metres behind it, while the wearer's left hand holds a screwdriver and right hand holds a hammer within arm's reach at 0.4 to 0.5 metres. In frame 5, the camera wearer turns and steps rightward, shifting the viewpoint so the rusty brake rotor sits on the left at roughly 0.6 metres and exposing a floor jack, red tool chest, and spare wheel on the floor to the right at 1.2 to 1.5 metres distance. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly separates the near overhead bar, mid-depth hands and wheel assembly, and distant workshop floor into distinct depth planes despite dark lighting and cluttered mechanical textures. However, the map is unreliable along the thin hammer head in frames 1 to 4 where the tool blends into the dark floor background, and in frame 5 where the distant floor jack and red toolbox lose sharp geometric boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's lower torso and extended arms at the bottom of the frame (0.2 to 0.5 metres from the camera, facing downward toward the vehicle assembly) while leaving almost all surrounding mechanical parts unlabelled. In frame 1 the map detects nothing at all, whereas in frames 2 to 4 a pink 'person' mask covers the wearer's crossed left and right arms and torso at the bottom center (with a small gap between the forearms) as the right hand moves closer to the left hand to strike the screwdriver. In frame 5, as the wearer turns rightward and steps back slightly, a brown 'person' mask covers the wearer's torso and right arm at the bottom right while the left hand at the bottom edge is largely missed. The map highlights the exact silhouette of the wearer's arms and clothing against the dark workshop floor where the RGB image has low contrast, but it is highly unreliable across the sequence. Specifically, it completely misses the wearer in frame 1, misclassifies the vertical metal vehicle fender on the left of frame 2 (at 0.3 metres) as a 'person', mislabels a spare car wheel and dark equipment at the top right of frame 5 (about 1.5 metres away) as a 'motorcycle', and fails to segment the brake rotor, tools, or toolbox.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks the 3D-projected joint locations of the camera wearer's left and right hands (in magenta) and fragmented upper-body links (in yellow) within arm's reach at roughly 0.4 to 0.6 metres below and in front of the camera, with no other people in the scene. In frame 1, the left hand is positioned above and to the left of the right hand (spaced about 0.15 metres apart) as both grip tools angled toward the brake backing plate to the upper right; across frames 2 to 4, the right hand moves upward and leftward to overlap directly beneath the left hand at the screwdriver handle. In frame 5, following the camera wearer's turn to the right, both hands drop toward the lower center-right and separate to about 0.2 metres apart, with the left hand lower and left of the right hand near the bottom frame boundary. This map reveals precise finger curl and wrist orientation during the overlapping tool interaction in frames 2 to 4 where the two hands and tool handles partially occlude each other in the RGB view. However, the pose estimation is unreliable for the full body because the egocentric downward viewpoint cuts off the wearer's head and shoulders, causing the yellow body skeleton to vanish completely in frames 2, 3, and 5 and appear only as distorted, truncated arm-to-torso lines in frames 1 and 4.
